job_description_info.job_description:
# Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI

**Company:** Quillstone Payments (fictional name; card-payment and business-tools provider)
**Location:** Hamburg, Germany (office-first)
**Team:** AI team within Customer Operations

## About the team

The Customer Operations organisation wants merchants to get help quickly and without friction. The AI team builds models and assistants that answer merchant questions, route tickets and help support agents. You will work with backend engineers, data scientists and product managers to take ideas from prototype to production.

## What you will do

- Build, deploy and operate AI and machine learning systems used by the support organisation
- Maintain pipelines for data processing, training and serving
- Fine-tune and evaluate models, including language models, for accuracy and cost
- Prepare and clean large text datasets
- Apply normal engineering discipline: version control, CI/CD and automated tests
- Integrate ML components into the wider product with other engineering teams

## Requirements

- Degree in machine learning, computer science or a related engineering field
- At least four years of experience as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production
- Experience with AI products such as chat assistants or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
- Software engineering skills for production systems: model serving, monitoring, data versioning
- Experience with a major cloud provider (AWS, GCP or Azure)
- Strong Python; familiarity with MLOps and orchestration tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow or an LLM-observability tool
- Experience with feature engineering and data ingestion pipelines

## Benefits

- Annual learning budget, employee share programme and company pension contribution
- Relocation support and subsidised meals
- Sabbatical after several years of service

company_info.company_description:
Quillstone Payments is a privately held financial-services company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Hamburg. It builds payment and money-management tools for small merchants, including payment terminals, a point-of-sale app and a business account. It serves millions of merchants across Europe and the Americas, with around 2,500 employees in approximately 20 offices. Its teams span product, engineering and operations; machine-learning work includes customer-support automation and fraud detection.

The company emphasizes ownership, teamwork and learning from mistakes. It values pragmatism, humility and candid feedback, and expects people to share context openly. Teams have autonomy to own their services and solve merchant problems, guided by shared principles rather than heavy processes. Quillstone is office-first, while allowing teams to agree on some flexible days. It supports development through training budgets, peer feedback, internal tech talks and twice-yearly development-plan reviews. The company also supports local business-education projects and publishes an annual inclusion report.

Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. I bring more than five years of experience in NLP and document classification, with hands-on work taking machine-learning models from research and prototyping into production. The opportunity to build and operate practical AI systems for merchant support—working from prototype through production—particularly interests me.

In my current role at Slavonica Document AI, I developed an automated document-classification model that achieved 94% accuracy across 23 classes for public-sector clients. I hold an MSc in Computer Science from Drava University and am currently pursuing PhD studies in Computer Science. I have also fine-tuned BERTić and XLM-R for named entity recognition in Croatian documents, and deployed models as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure ML and Azure App Service. Using Python, I have applied MLOps practices with MLflow for experiment tracking, model versioning and registry, and production monitoring. To support reliable operations, I introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry and established production monitoring for data drift with weekly reporting. This experience aligns closely with your need to build, serve and monitor AI systems in production.

My earlier work includes building text-classification models for customer complaints using TF-IDF, logistic regression and fastText, as well as developing churn-prediction models with gradient boosting and LightGBM.
